title: A Galois-invariant clopen partition descends to the original scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $L/k$ be a Galois extension [def-pc-field-extension], possibly of infinite degree: it is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and normal (the minimal polynomial over $k$ of every element of $L$ splits in $L$). Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], put $X_L=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-base-change], and let $p:X_L\to X$ be the projection. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(L/k)$ write $\sigma_X=\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose $P,Q\subseteq X_L$ are nonempty open and closed subsets satisfying $X_L=P\amalg Q$ and $\sigma_X(P)=P$, $\sigma_X(Q)=Q$ for every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(L/k)$. Then there is a unique ordered pair $(P_0,Q_0)$ of nonempty open and closed subsets of $X$ with
$$
X=P_0\amalg Q_0,\qquad p^{-1}(P_0)=P,\qquad p^{-1}(Q_0)=Q.
$$
No connectedness, quasi-compactness, or finite-type hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 038B, lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois, applied to both members of a partition; the clopen partition descent used immediately after the displayed intersection/union construction in lemma-tricky. Surjectivity of the field-extension projection gives disjointness, covering, and uniqueness.

proof.text: The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] to its pullback along $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its projection to $X$ is $p$, so $p$ is surjective. This uses no finiteness hypothesis on the extension or on $X$.

source.place: Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective, applied to the field-extension spectrum map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-galois-invariant-closed-subset-descends] with $\bar k=L$ first to $\bar T=P$ and then to $\bar T=Q$. Both subsets are closed and invariant under precisely the action in that statement, and $L/k$ is possibly infinite Galois as required. We obtain closed subsets $P_0,Q_0\subseteq X$ with $p^{-1}(P_0)=P$ and $p^{-1}(Q_0)=Q$.

source.place: Tag 038B, lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois, applied separately to P and Q.

proof.text: For each $x\in X$, choose $y\in X_L$ with $p(y)=x$ by Step 1. The inverse-image equalities in Step 2 say $x\in P_0$ if and only if $y\in P$, and $x\in Q_0$ if and only if $y\in Q$. Exactly one alternative holds because $X_L=P\amalg Q$. Thus $X=P_0\amalg Q_0$. Each member is the complement of the other closed member, hence is open as well as closed.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, paragraph after the displayed intersection/union: descent of both closed members yields a clopen partition. Set-theoretic details expanded.

proof.text: Choose $y\in P$; then $p(y)\in P_0$ by Step 2, so $P_0$ is nonempty. The same argument with $Q$ shows $Q_0$ is nonempty. For uniqueness, if $A,B\subseteq X$ have the prescribed inverse images, choose for every $x\in X$ a lift $y$ as in Step 1. Then $x\in A\iff y\in P\iff x\in P_0$ and $x\in B\iff y\in Q\iff x\in Q_0$. Set extensionality gives $A=P_0$ and $B=Q_0$, proving uniqueness of the ordered pair.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_clopen_partition_of_galois_invariant (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] [IsGalois k L] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] (P Q : Set ↥(pullback (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))))) (hPne : P.Nonempty) (hQne : Q.Nonempty) (hP : IsClopen P) (hQ : IsClopen Q) (hdisjoint : Disjoint P Q) (hcover : P ∪ Q = Set.univ) (hPinvariant : ∀ σ : L ≃ₐ[k] L, (baseChangeMap (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) (specAlgEquivOver σ)) '' P = P) (hQinvariant : ∀ σ : L ≃ₐ[k] L, (baseChangeMap (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) (specAlgEquivOver σ)) '' Q = Q) : ∃! R : Set X × Set X, R.1.Nonempty ∧ R.2.Nonempty ∧ IsClopen R.1 ∧ IsClopen R.2 ∧ Disjoint R.1 R.2 ∧ R.1 ∪ R.2 = Set.univ ∧ (pullback.fst (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))) ⁻¹' R.1 = P ∧ (pullback.fst (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))) ⁻¹' R.2 = Q
